facts.value: Businesses often have important intellectual property that needs protection from competitors for the company to stay profitable.

facts.value: This could require patents, copyrights, trademarks, or preservation of trade secrets.

facts.value: Most businesses have names, logos, and similar branding techniques that could benefit from trademarking.

facts.value: Patents and copyrights in the United States are largely governed by federal law, while trade secrets and trademarking are mostly a matter of state law.
facts.programme_association: Business Communication Degree Concentration | ASU Online

facts.value: A business needs protection in every jurisdiction in which they are concerned about competitors.

facts.value: Many countries are signatories to international treaties concerning intellectual property.
facts.programme_association: Business Communication Degree Concentration | ASU Online

facts.value: Companies registered in countries that are signatories to treaties are subject to national laws bound by these treaties.

facts.value: To protect trade secrets, companies may require employees to sign noncompete clauses which will impose limitations on an employee's interactions with stakeholders and competitors.
